speaker: Other
text: This is Supreme Court case number CVA-19-025, Juan P. San Nicolas and John J. Sablon, petitioners, appellants, versus Edward Byrne in his official capacity as the Director for the Department of Administration, Respondent Appellee, and Guam Fire Department Real Party and Interest Appellee. Appearing for the petitioners, appellants, is Attorney Jacqueline Titano Terlahi. Appearing for the Respondent Appellee and Real Party and Interest is Attorney James L. Canto. The panel consists of Chief Justice F. Philip Carballito, Associate Justice Robert J. Torres, and Associate Justice Catherine A. Merriman. Attorney Terlahi reserves 10 minutes.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: Thank you, Madam Clerk. At this time, Attorney Terlahi, you are recognized.

speaker: jacqueterlaje
text: Buenas den hafa adai. May it please the court, Chief Justice Carballito, Justice Torres, and Justice Merriman. For 20 years, firefighter Juan San Nicolas and firefighter Sablon have asserted the rights afforded to them under Guam law. After 20 years and after two separate writ proceedings, an administrative proceeding before the Civil Service Commission, a desk audit, and a judicial review process in the Superior Court of Guam, they finally sought from the Superior Court the second writ, which is the subject of this particular appeal, which is to hold that they, to find that they hold permanently and should be promoted to a fire specialist position pursuant to 10 GCA section 72-107. What's extremely important in this case is to remember that these firefighters did not put themselves in a temporary position in excess of five years. It was the Guam Fire Department who assigned them to a position in the Fire Prevention Bureau. The lower court, when it made a determination, a factual determination, that firefighters Sablon and San Nicolas did not occupy the position of fire specialist, the lower court abused its discretion. It abused its discretion for two important reasons. The first is because there is a race judicata doctrine application in this case. As I set forth at the beginning in this case, firefighters San Nicolas and Sablon sought review before the CSC, sought review before the Superior Court. When those particular avenues were foreclosed to them, they sought a writ of mandamus, which was granted to them. Following 15 years of litigation, firefighters San Nicolas and Sablon lost their determination at the CSC. They initially sought to be held to the position of fire captain. It was the Civil Service Commission who made the factual determination that they did not perform the duties of fire captain, but that they perform the duties of a fire specialist. As a result of that finding at the Civil Service Commission, the firefighters then sought the ministerial act of the Department of Administration to perform its obligations as set forth by 72-107. Only at that time...

text: If I may interrupt at this time, the Superior Court, you raised the issue of breast judicata, which is a substantive issue that, at least in my mind, that is before us. text: None of those statutes are applicable to these circumstances, Chief Justice Torres. As set forth by Chief Justice Carbolito, hindsight is always much better. speaker: philipcarbullido
text: And so- As the government points out, Attorney Tarulagi, in reference to the first case, SB018, point hyphen one zero, although the Civil Service Commission's finding or decision was that the firefighters were performing duties as a fire service specialist, since that was the decision and the writ that was taken as a result of after that ruling, the government points out that it could have been raised that with that conclusion, that then they were entitled to the benefits of 10 GCA 72107. text: And Your Honor, what you have in SB189-10 is the Superior Court of Guam holding that 10 GCA 72107 was not within that particular writ of mandate process, that that court had not considered that issue and the court was not going to consider that issue because it did not feel that that issue was before it. speaker: philipcarbullido

text: Essentially, Your Honor, that's exactly what happened in these proceedings. speaker: roberttorres
text: When the court made its decision that the request for a writ is appropriate in a separate action, they made a finding that the request in the renewed peremptory writ was different in the claim and relief than what was initially requested in the first verified petition. speaker: jacqueterlaje
text: The major fact that is different is that we have a factual finding by the Civil Service Commission that the firefighters were performing as fire specialists. In this writ of review, we are asking the court to find that the writ of mandamus was appropriate because the action below was specifically about whether or not DOA had performed its obligations under the statute. Two different entities may arise from the same set of facts, but the ultimate fact that made the change to lead to these proceedings was a determination of fact. That fact was that the firefighters were performing as fire specialists on a temporary basis for more than five years. That's where these particular firefighters were drawn into this statute, which granted them the right to promotion, which was a new right that was established by statute. speaker: roberttorres
text: Had the CSC- So you're saying there's not an identity of the parties? In one case, it was the CSC, and in the other case, it's the Department of Administration? text: Well, Your Honor, technically speaking, the Department of Administration with GFD were parties in the civil service proceedings. In one case, it was the factual determination of whether or not the firefighters were performing in job one or job two. We were advancing the theory that they were performing as fire captains. We failed at that particular process. And it was the CSC who made the determination that they were not performing as fire captains, they were performing as fire specialists. So as a result of that determination, a new obligation was imposed on the Department of Administration by 10 GCA 72-107. As a result of that finding of the CSC, DOA then was compelled by Guam law to promote ministerially these two firefighters because there was a finding that they had been performing in the fire specialist position in excess of five years.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: And that's where I have a little problem, Attorney Terlagi, is when there was that determination that the firefighters here were performing as a fire service specialist. speaker: jacqueterlaje

speaker: jamescanto
text: Mr. Chief Justice, Associate Justices, may it please the court, respond in appellee DOA and real party in interest GFD would respectfully urge the court to affirm the lower court's finding and holding and decision in SP 88-17 for several reasons. And the first being the res judicata issue, which has been raised quite a bit by the court just now. The fact that the CSC did enter a, render a final judgment on the merits, that there was an identity of issues and identity of parties. And alternatively, as has been pointed out by the court, the issue regarding 10 GCA section 72-107 could have been raised at the CSC level. And this is where I think there may be a miscommunication between counsel and the court on this issue. The reason that the trial court in SP 189-10 said that it had no jurisdiction to hear the argument being made under section 72-107 at that time was because petitioners did not exhaust their administrative remedies on that issue below. And so that issue should have been brought to the civil service commission. However, the petitioners flatly rejected that finding by the civil service commission, that as the court in, I believe 189-10 pointed out, if not SP 8817, that petitioners, once the CSC found that they were performing duties at the level of a fire specialist, the petitioners rejected that seeking to be compensated, if not promoted as fire captains. And so that issue was crystallized at the CSC level and the petitioners did nothing to go back and exhaust their administrative remedies to ensure that there was a waiver of sovereign immunity so that the court in SP 189-10 could be able to hear that issue that they would be advancing. And that could have taken the form of a grievance which would have been the proper course. But that's another reason why the lower courts holding should be affirmed. And that is in terms of the statutes of limitations violations, three of them that were violated by the petitioners in the case. One, starting with that 20 day statute of limitations imposed by DOA personnel rule 5.014 D as to when to bring the issue forward to DOA for the desk audit, they waited four years instead of 20 days. Then once they received the determination by DOA that talked about compensation, as opposed to promotion, the petitioners should have, according to DOA personnel rule 5.014 F have appealed that determination to the CSC within 20 days. Instead, they waited 14 months and violated the second statute of limitations that would apply to them in that regard. And then third, even as the trial court pointed out, the statute of limitations in 7GCA section 11305, which is a three-year statute of limitations to bring the issue before the court because of an obligation created by law, they failed at that as well in terms of SP88-17, which is the case before this court currently. And they violated the statute of limitations to come forward and file that case, even though they were instructed by the, as council submits, that they were instructed by the trial court in SP189-10 to file another writ. They didn't do that within the statute of limitations for doing so. Even the court in SP189-10 gave them great latitude and benefit of doubt to say, well, because it was a continuing violation, they were finally promoted in 2008, they would have had three years from that time to file an action in superior court. Instead, and that's why the court in SP189-10 entertained it because that was in 2010. So even by that argument, their ability to come before the court would have lapsed in at the very latest, the end of 2011, beginning of 2012. However, the petitioners did not come forward and file an action that is before the court currently until more than five years later in 2017. Another reason why that statute of limitations was violated and the reason for which the action before the court now should be affirmed in terms of the lower court's holding, if for not that reason alone. Another reason why we asked the court to affirm the lower court's ruling applies to the failure to exhaust administrative remedies on behalf of the petitioners. As I've explained somewhat, and which do connote jurisdictional problems as statutes have proposed because of the necessity for waiver of sovereign immunity to bring this suit. And I don't mean that in terms of a drive by jurisdictional ruling as this court noted, say in Castino versus TC Corporation, because it is a suit against the government for which of course the waiver of sovereign immunity must be expressed only made by legislature and strictly construed by the courts. And those would have included filing that grievance before the civil service commission on the issue of 10 GCA section 72-107. If not to move the civil service commission to reconsider its decision or to file for an administrative review of job classification, which is what the lower courts have found is really at issue here, that they're seeking job classification redetermination for an actual promotion, as opposed to being compensated for performing the duties of that position. Also the 10 GCA section 72-107 simply does not apply to the petitioner's facts. The petitioners in their opening brief go to great lengths to say that somehow the civil service commission found that they had occupied the position of fire specialist. And those key words, occupied the position are repeatedly used by petitioners in their brief, because they know that that is the operative language of the statute 72-107. And they can't advance their case without applying the facts in that regard. The problem for that-

text: Don't you think someone serving in a position for five consecutive years is occupying that position?

text: No, your honor, with all due respect, it's simply performing the duties. speaker: roberttorres
text: But couldn't we interpret it in a way to reward an employee who's performing the work of that position to which he wasn't promoted or appointed? text: Well, this, okay. 72-107, when you look at it, you can infer that it was meant to remedy something that was never done properly under 4117 to allow, and apparently it must be there to address people who have been temporarily appointed, formally temporarily appointed to positions for much longer than the 90 days or 180 days. text: Not for five years. But like I was saying, that's why 72-107, it's very apparent that this is to remedy a past error because people were, in order to qualify under this, must have been appointed for longer. And also it could be argued that this is the specific statute that would govern the general being 4117. I know petitioners have rejected the application of that statute to their circumstance. And it says it right here in the title, rendering appointments permanent, your honor. You can't render something permanent as an appointment if there was no appointment to begin with. It does not, the statute doesn't say that anyone who performs the duties for five years will be automatically promoted. And you can't perform duties on a temporary basis because that just doesn't, that language doesn't apply. It doesn't make sense when referring to performing duties. An appointment on a temporary basis does and act by the hiring authority to detail them or actually appoint them.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: So shouldn't it have some language to say that notwithstanding 4117, the department head can appoint an employee on a temporary basis in excess of 180 days. Shouldn't there be some type of triggering language that will authorize this? Because I think you have been the circumstance of the facts that we have in front of us where the two firefighters here were performing fire service specialists duties in excess of five years. And the department has number one, chosen not to compensate them for this additional because there's no GG1 that will authorize payroll to pay them for the excess service. And so, but you're saying, well, despite us having this expectation, you have to object in order for us to then be required to pay you. It just seems that there are equities here that are called into question. Should that issue be reached?

speaker: jamescanto
text: Understood, your honor. And yes, I would agree that it would be ideal if 72107 did acknowledge and attempt to reconcile itself with 4117, that's not what happened here. And again, it brings into the question as the court kind of hinted at initially as to the legitimacy of 72107 itself to be able to circumvent the competitive hiring process. Because even given the perceived inequities, the petitioners place themselves in this position. Like I said, your honor, they could have refused to do those duties until they were properly compensated or put in a position where they would be mandated to perform the duties and be properly compensated for them. But they didn't do that. They didn't seek a job classification. Well, they did seek a promotion to fire captain initially, but that was way beyond the pale in terms of, because they weren't on all fours of that position in terms of duties they were in fact performing, but they were in fact more than those of firefighter one. But they didn't pursue those avenues sufficiently or at all really, except for in hindsight and retrospect to be able to resolve the inequities in a way that the court is now perceiving them. And they were in fact compensated.

speaker: roberttorres
text: You seem to suggest that the absurd result that would occur under this situation is employees would do sort of self-promotion and just do the work without any temporary detail assignment into that position. But that's not really the facts of this case, right? I mean, here they were actually performing duties that were requested of them. Although they're, you know, in your position, you're saying they weren't temporarily appointed or they weren't appointed to that position, even temporarily.

speaker: jamescanto
text: Governor, I am not suggesting that they were performing duties surreptitiously and without the knowledge of their employer. I wouldn't even venture to suggest that because I sincerely doubt that that was what was happening. But it doesn't-

speaker: roberttorres
text: That was what you suggested would make, why there was an absurd result that could occur if it was interpreted in the manner that was suggested by the petitioner.

speaker: jamescanto
text: That was suggested in the lower court by another counsel with my office. And in terms of general application of the argument, I would stand by that, Your Honor. That can't be the measure by which we seek to properly compensate others. They can't create their own job. But I'm not suggesting that that was necessarily the case here. I don't know for a fact, but I have no reason to assume that they were not conducting those duties without permission. Another problem for the petitioners in this case and why the court should affirm is not just because of the problems with the application of 72107 to their circumstances, but also because they resign, as the court pointed out. Now, whereas counsel like to characterize this euphemistically as a break in service, they resign. And that is an open and unambiguous waiver of the right to continue to pursue the issue at the administrative level, like they should have. Even if they did get rehired and they were rehired to different positions than they were in when they left. So it doesn't make sense to be able to come back and promote them from a position that they are not in anymore. Also, just to address the petitioner's argument that somehow the respondents and real party interests are bound by judicial admissions. I hope the court would give this no more than cursory analysis. I think it's very clear, even as the trial court pointed out that the supposed admissions that were made by respondent and real party interests were only quasi admissions, not judicial admissions that are considered binding. They were also admissions regarding issues of legal opinion and fact, whether or not according to 72-107, the petitioners occupied the position of fire specialists. Whereas in other portions in all pleadings and the motions to follow, which continued were such that there were other contradictory responses that the respondent and real party interests always continually denied that 72-107 applies. And your honors, I would rest on that. We ask that the court affirm the lower courts holding in this case. And unless the court has any other questions of myself, I would concede the floor. And thank you.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: Thank you, Mr. Canto. If there are no questions for Deputy Attorney General Canto, I will ask Attorney Terlaghi. You have a few minutes to complete.

speaker: jacqueterlaje
text: Yes, thank you, your honors. What's important in this case, as you hear from the government's position is that the government never denies that it put the employees in a particular position to perform duties above and beyond the position that they were hired for. In this particular case, the GSD never denied that they appointed firefighters to Nicholas and Sabwan to the Fire Prevention Bureau and required that they perform the duties of fire specialists for more than five years. In fact, the Guam Fire Department had them perform duties as fire specialists from 2001 through 2008. At best, the public policy mandates that the court declined to award the government for its bad conduct, especially in this case, where the government had denied its obligation to the employees for a 20 year period. The employees have continually requested that the Guam Fire Department abide by its obligations imposed by law. And at every juncture, the government has placed obstacles before it. Now, the government sets forth that the employees waited too long to argue. Well, the employees made a complaint initially to their supervisors and it led to a desk audit in 2005. Yes, albeit four years, but following those four years, they continued to perform duties for another four years through 2008. And what the government's position in this case is simply that they should not be held responsible for employees who perform duties that are required of them and in contravention of Guam law. Guam Fire Department was fully aware of its obligations not to temporarily assign employees to positions that are outside of their employment. They should not be rewarded public policy mandates that the court impose equity and award the firefighters what is imposed on DOA under the statute. And that's promotion to the fire specialist position. Your Honor, I believe I am out of time.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: All right. Thank you, Attorney Terlai. Thank you, Deputy Attorney General Canto. At this time, the court will take the arguments under advisement. We thank you for your presentation and the court stands adjourned.

speaker: jacqueterlaje
text: To dismiss, Your Honor.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: Thank you, counsels.
